title: On the ledge
imageAlt: The cub hangs from the edge of a snowy ledge.
sentences: I reached for berries
and the snow broke under me.
A tree caught me
before I hit the ground.

title: In the branches
imageAlt: The cub sits among the evergreen's branches.
sentences: The tree gave me seeds
when my belly was empty.
That night I found a warm bed
up in its branches.

title: A spring morning
imageAlt: The evergreen and the cub sit beside a patch of soil.
sentences: That spring, my friend gave me
a little toy made from a pinecone.
We put a seed in the ground
and watched a baby tree grow.

title: The chip bag
imageAlt: The older cub peers into a bright bag of potato chips.
sentences: A crow dropped a bag of chips,
and I wanted to find more.
My friend tried to stop me,
but I went off on my own.

title: At the campsite
imageAlt: The bear searches a pile of food and rubbish at a campsite.
sentences: I made it across the river
and found a camp full of food.
I kept eating
even after the sun went down.

title: After dark
imageAlt: The bear sleeps beside the rubbish as an orange ember glows.
sentences: A pinecone I tossed
knocked a hot coal into the rubbish.
I was already asleep
when the fire began to spread.

title: Across the gap
imageAlt: The fallen tree reaches towards the bear, who is still holding an armful of rubbish.
sentences: The tree made a bridge for me
by falling across the gap.
I had to drop what I was carrying
before I could grab its branch.

title: On the far side
imageAlt: The bear watches the burning tree fall into the canyon.
sentences: I hugged my friend
in the middle of the bridge.
The tree got me to safety
and fell into the canyon.

title: Among the ashes
imageAlt: The bear holds the pinecone toy with a green shoot growing out of it.
sentences: I thought I had lost everything
until I saw a green shoot on my old toy.
I planted it
right in the middle of the old stump.

title: Years later
imageAlt: The grown bear holds up a pinecone for a little cub in the branches of the new tree.
sentences: Years later, I met a cub
as small as I'd once been.
I held out a pinecone for him
in the branches of the tree I'd grown.
